_comment: Input and request validation -- feature 19. Two owner decisions
(019-input-validation.md VALID-DEC-01 + VALID-DEC-02).
There are TWO validators in every language, and BOTH are kept:
(a) a chainable request-body Validator (required/email/min_length/
max_length/integer/min/max/in_list/regex -> errors()/is_valid()) that
is ADVISORY -- the caller inspects it and decides; and
(b) ORM field validation that runs ON SAVE and is ENFORCED -- an invalid
model makes save() return false and writes NOTHING (never touches the
driver).
VALID-DEC-01 (fix the UNPROVEN controls -- highest value):
- VALID-PY-UNTESTED: Python's request Validator (9 rules) was BEHAVIOURALLY
UNTESTED -- tests/test_data_validator.py and tests/test_form_validator.py
were 2-line `assert True` PLACEHOLDERS named as if they covered it (worse
than a skip). Both DELETED; test_validation_contract.py now covers every
rule pos AND neg.
- VALID-PHP-ENFORCE-UNTESTED: PHP's validate-on-save ENFORCEMENT path had
NO test (validate() was tested only in isolation). ValidationContractTest
now declares a $fields-constrained model, calls save() on invalid data,
and asserts save() === false AND a real COUNT(*) === 0.
- VALID-RUBY-NULLONLY (tests): Ruby's Validator rules max_length/max/
in_list/regex were untested; validation_contract_spec now covers them.
VALID-DEC-02 (close the enforcement gaps + unify the vocabulary):
- VALID-RUBY-NULLONLY (fix): Ruby's ORM validate() was NULL-ONLY (length,
type and format were declared but NEVER enforced on save), so Ruby wrote
an over-length/wrong-format value the other three reject. validate() now
enforces required + length + numeric range + format + numeric type; the
field DSL gained required:/min_length:/max_length:/pattern:/min:/max:; and
the dead validate_fields (a zero-caller re-implementation of the null
check) was DELETED. `length:` stays a DDL sizing hint, never validated
(parity with PHP's `length`).
- VALID-NODE-PUT-NOVALIDATE: Node's AutoCrud PUT did NO request-body
validation (only POST called validate()). PUT now calls validate(body,
fields, isUpdate=true) and rejects invalid input with 422; the
partial-update mode (isUpdate) is wired into baseModel.save() too, so an
update does not spuriously require unrelated fields. Proven over a REAL
node:http socket against a REAL SQLite database.
- VALID-TWO-MESSAGES: the request Validator and the ORM validator emitted
DIFFERENT strings for the same rule (PHP ORM "name: is required" vs the
Validator's "name is required"; Node ORM "does not match required
pattern" vs the Validator's "does not match the required format"). They
now speak ONE canonical vocabulary -- the Node request-Validator wording,
field-prefixed with a SPACE -- across BOTH validators in ALL FOUR:
required    -> "<field> is required"
email       -> "<field> must be a valid email address"
min_length  -> "<field> must be at least N characters"
max_length  -> "<field> must be at most N characters"
integer     -> "<field> must be an integer"
min         -> "<field> must be at least N"
max         -> "<field> must be at most N"
in_list     -> "<field> must be one of [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"]"  (compact JSON)
regex       -> "<field> does not match the required format"
PHP dropped the colon; Node's ORM regex wording changed; Python and Ruby
in_list now render the allowed set as compact JSON (json.dumps compact /
to_json) matching Node's JSON.stringify and PHP's json_encode.
BREAKING (all correctness fixes, documented in the changelog): Ruby now
enforces length/type/format on save (previously-accepted input now rejected);
Node's AutoCrud PUT now validates (a previously-accepted invalid update is now
422); the unified vocabulary changes some error strings (PHP colon removed,
Node ORM regex wording, Python/Ruby in_list JSON).
SCOPE NOTE (reported, not widened): only Node's AutoCrud auto-wires the
request Validator (POST already, and now PUT). Python/PHP/Ruby AutoCrud do NOT
auto-wire request-body validation -- that is feature-27 (AutoCrud) scope, so
the AutoCrud-PUT invariant names the Node suite alone.
NO MOCKS anywhere: the request-rule cases are pure logic over their inputs;
the save()-writes-nothing cases drive a REAL SQLite database and assert a real
COUNT(*) after the refused save; the Node AutoCrud PUT case drives a REAL
node:http socket against a REAL SQLite database. Each invariant names a REAL
suite file per framework carrying the SAME case names in each language's own
idiom, normalised + matched by scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py. Mutation-
proven: disable Ruby max_length -> the over-length + max-length-message cases
go RED; disable Node's PUT validate -> the PUT-422 case goes RED (the invalid
update writes through, 200); stub PHP validate() to return [] -> the
enforcement + message cases go RED. All restore GREEN.
feature: 19 - Input and request validation (VALID-DEC-01 fix the untested validators: Python placeholders, PHP enforcement, Ruby rules; VALID-DEC-02 Ruby richer ORM validate, Node AutoCrud PUT validation + partial-update, unified message vocabulary)

invariants.rule: The chainable request-body Validator enforces all nine rules -- required, email, min_length, max_length, integer, min, max, in_list, regex -- each with a POSITIVE case (valid input passes, is_valid() true) AND a NEGATIVE case (invalid input reports the canonical message and is_valid() false); errors() carries one {field, message} per failed rule. Identical rule set and canonical wording in all four frameworks.
invariants.why: VALID-PY-UNTESTED: Python's Validator had ZERO real coverage -- two `assert True` placeholders named as if they covered it (deleted here). VALID-RUBY-NULLONLY (tests): Ruby's max_length/max/in_list/regex were untested. Pure-logic over the input -- no database, the plan's cheapest suite. Each negative case pins the CANONICAL message string so it also anchors VALID-TWO-MESSAGES on the request-validator side (in_list renders compact JSON in every language).
cases: required rule passes a present value and reports a missing one
email rule passes a valid address and reports an invalid one
min length rule passes a long value and reports a short one
max length rule passes a short value and reports a long one
integer rule passes an integer and reports a non integer
min rule passes a value above the minimum and reports one below
max rule passes a value below the maximum and reports one above
in list rule passes an allowed value and reports a disallowed one
regex rule passes a matching value and reports a non matching one
is valid reflects whether any rule failed

invariants.rule: ORM field validation runs ON SAVE and is ENFORCED: a model that violates a declared constraint (required missing, over max length, out of numeric range, pattern mismatch) has save() return false AND writes NOTHING -- a real COUNT(*) of the table after the refused save is zero; a fully valid model saves and writes exactly one row. Proven against a real SQLite database in all four frameworks.
invariants.why: VALID-PHP-ENFORCE-UNTESTED: PHP's enforcement path (validate() -> save() returns false, writes nothing) had NO test. VALID-RUBY-NULLONLY: Ruby's ORM validate() was NULL-ONLY, so an over-length/out-of-range/wrong-format value was written silently -- Ruby now enforces the shared richness (length/type/format/range). The COUNT(*)-after-refused-save is the real-DB proof that nothing reached the driver (no mock, no smoke test). Mutation-proven: stub the validator -> every violation case goes RED (the row is written).
cases: a required violation makes save return false and writes nothing
an over length value makes save return false and writes nothing
an out of range value makes save return false and writes nothing
a pattern violation makes save return false and writes nothing
a valid model saves and writes one row

invariants.rule: The request-body Validator and the ORM validator emit the IDENTICAL canonical message string for the same rule on the same field -- required, min_length, max_length, min, max and regex -- using the Node request-Validator vocabulary ("<field> is required", "<field> must be at least N characters", "<field> must be at most N characters", "<field> must be at least N", "<field> must be at most N", "<field> does not match the required format"). A client keying on a message matches either validator, in all four frameworks.
invariants.why: VALID-TWO-MESSAGES: the two validators drifted apart (PHP ORM "name: is required" vs Validator "name is required"; Node ORM "does not match required pattern" vs Validator "does not match the required format") -- a client keying on one wording would not match the other. Each case triggers the SAME violation through BOTH validators and asserts the messages are byte-identical AND equal to the locked canonical string. The Node request Validator is the reference the others already cited; the seven other surfaces were aligned to it.
cases: required emits the same canonical message from both validators
min length emits the same canonical message from both validators
max length emits the same canonical message from both validators
min emits the same canonical message from both validators
max emits the same canonical message from both validators
regex emits the same canonical message from both validators

invariants.rule: Node's AutoCrud PUT validates the request body (previously only POST did): an invalid update is rejected with HTTP 422 and writes nothing, while the partial-update mode (isUpdate=true) lets a valid partial update through WITHOUT spuriously requiring the unrelated required fields the row already carries; POST still rejects an invalid body with 422. Proven over a real node:http socket against a real SQLite database. Node-only: Python/PHP/Ruby AutoCrud do not auto-wire request-body validation (feature-27 scope, reported not widened).
invariants.why: VALID-NODE-PUT-NOVALIDATE: the AutoCrud update path performed NO validation, so a PUT could write type/length/pattern/required-violating data a create would reject; and the validator's isUpdate partial-update mode was wired into no write path (save() always passed isUpdate=false, enforcing required even on updates). The PUT now calls validate(body, fields, true) and 422s; baseModel.save() passes the real isUpdate. Proven end to end over a real socket + real SQLite -- the 422 status and the untouched row come back off the wire. Mutation-proven: remove the PUT validate -> the invalid update returns 200 and writes through (RED).
cases: autocrud put rejects an invalid body with 422
autocrud put allows a partial update without requiring unrelated fields
autocrud post still rejects an invalid body with 422
